descriptionChirho: Describing something or someone as difficult, unyielding, harsh, or severe — applied to persons (a hard master, Mt 25:24), conditions (hard sayings, Jn 6:60), natural forces (harsh winds, Jas 3:4), and speech (harsh words, Jude 1:15). Multilingual evidence confirms a unified semantic field: Spanish 'duro/fuertes/duras' all denote harshness; Hindi 'कठिन/कठोर/प्रचण्ड' range from difficult to fierce; Arabic 'صَعْبٌ/قَاسٍ/عاصِفَة/القاسية' span hard, cruel, stormy, harsh; Korean '엄한/어려운/거센/완악한' cover strict, difficult, fierce, obstinate; Swahili 'vigumu/ngumu/mkali/magumu' all convey hardness or severity. The grammatical case differences (nominative, genitive masculine/neuter plural) do not indicate separate senses but merely inflectional variation of the same core meaning of hardness and harshness.
